title: CHAPTER FORTY. On the humans obligation to death
latin: CAPUT QUADRAGESIMUM, De obligatione hominis ad mortem. HAec de permissione peccati: OBLIGATIO hominis ad mortem est eius poenalis conditio, in quam Dei lapso illius offensi iusto iudicio redactus est, ut maledictioni aeternae sit obnoxius. Ex capitis 37 aph. 2 patet, post dogma de permissione peccati locum esse doctrinae de obligatione hominis lapsi ad mortem seu poenae subitionem, de qua Gen. 2:17. Supponit autem haec obligatio partim offensionem Dei ex peccato, quod ante se habet Dei prohibitionem ac poenae denunciationem, siquidem homo legi Dei non obediret. Ex offensione nascitur in Deo affectus vindicandi, quo videlicet Deus appetit peccatori pro malo culpae tribuere malum poenae. Ex vindictae vero affectu et reatu seu obligatione ad poenam sequitur ipsa poena, cuius aequitas ex reatu, inflictio vero ex affectu vindictae seu ira et rigore iustitiae, quae coniungitur cum veritate Dei in servanda comminatione, nisi temperetur nova gratia, qua maledictio aeterna vertatur in benedictionem aeternam coniunctam cum castigatione temporaria.
english: CHAPTER FORTY. On the humans obligation to death.

Thus far concerning the permission of sin: the OBLIGATION of the human to death is his penal condition, into which by the just judgment of God offended by that fall he has been reduced, so that he is liable to eternal curse. From chapter 37, aphorism 2, it is plain that after the dogma of the permission of sin there is place for the doctrine of the fallen humans obligation to death or the undergoing of punishment, of which Genesis 2:17 speaks.

This obligation presupposes partly Gods offense from sin, which has before it Gods prohibition and the denunciation of punishment if the human should not obey Gods law. From offense there is born in God the affection of avenging, by which God seeks to assign to the sinner for the evil of fault the evil of punishment. And from the affection of vengeance and from guilt or obligation to punishment follows the punishment itself, whose equity is from guilt, but whose infliction is from the affection of vengeance or the wrath and rigor of justice, which is joined with Gods truth in keeping the threat — unless it is tempered by new grace, by which eternal curse is turned into eternal blessing joined with temporary chastisement.

title: II–III. Penal condition: eternal curse or paternal chastisement; curse remains on unbelievers
latin: II. Poenalis conditio igitur est maledictionis aeternae aut castigationis paternae. III. Maledictio aeterna est, quae propter culpam humani generis in Christum translata, eos manet qui hunc non recipiunt. Res clara est Marc. 16:16: Qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur. Ioh. 3:36: Qui vero non assentitur Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum. Apoc. 21:8: Formidolosis autem et incredulis et exsecrabilibus et homicidis et scortatoribus et veneficis et idololatris et omnibus mendacibus (id est, Christum, veritatem non recipientibus) portio est in stagno ubi ardet ignis et sulphur, quod est mors secunda. Huius typus fuit eiectio e paradiso, quatenus paradisus fuit caelestis domicilii figura. De maledictione vero et morte aeterna supra egimus lib. 2 cap. XV, quae eos duntaxat manet qui testimonium Christi non recipiunt.
english: II. The penal condition therefore is of eternal curse or of paternal chastisement. III. Eternal curse is that which, the guilt of the human race having been transferred onto Christ, remains for those who do not receive Him. The matter is clear in Mark 16:16: But whoever does not believe will be condemned. John 3:36: But whoever does not assent to the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him. Revelation 21:8: But for the fearful and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and fornicators and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars (that is, those not receiving Christ, the truth) their portion is in the lake where fire and sulphur burn, which is the second death. A type of this was the ejection from paradise, insofar as paradise was a figure of the heavenly dwelling. Of eternal curse and death we treated above in Book II chapter 15; it remains only for those who do not receive the testimony of Christ.

title: IV–V. Paternal chastisement for those looking to the womans seed; of the first parents and of posterity
latin: IV. Castigatio paterna est, qua peccatoribus ad benedictum semen mulieris respicientibus vetus ipsorum natura per crucem temporariam adultus instar reformatur. Hinc Apostolus Rom. 8:1: Nulla igitur nunc est condemnatio iis qui in Christo Iesu, qui non secundum carnem ambulant, sed secundum spiritum. Et v. 28-29. V. Est vero haec protoplastorum aut posterorum. Protoplastis irrogata sunt: expulsio e paradiso, labor, dolor partus, subiectio, mors temporalis (Gen. 3:16-19). Posteris eadem transmissae sunt cum originali peccato.
english: IV. Paternal chastisement is that by which, for sinners looking to the blessed seed of the woman, their old nature is reformed through a temporary cross after the manner of an adult. Hence the Apostle in Romans 8:1: There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit. And verses 28-29. V. And this is either of the first parents or of posterity. On the first parents were laid: expulsion from paradise, labor, pain of childbirth, subjection, temporal death (Genesis 3:16-19). To posterity the same were transmitted with original sin.

title: VIII–XI. Eves fourfold penalty; natural and spiritual state after the fall
latin: VIII. EVAE quatuor habet partes poena: multiplicatio doloris in partu, desiderium ad virum, dominatio viri, et mors. Adami poena: maledictio terrae, labor in sudore, reditus in pulverem. XI. Quantum ad statum naturalem, soluta sibi permissa est vis naturae, nec amplius peculiari illa Dei providentia qua sub statu innocentiae regitur ac reprimitur, qua videlicet ne molestiae quicquam hominibus inferret cohibebatur, ut supra docuimus. Quantum ad statum spiritualem est partim amissio primae DEI gratiae et faventiae, partim, quae hanc secuta est, boni Dei Spiritus contristatio et ab homine discessio, quam continenter excepit mentis caligo et agnoia seu voluntatis obliquitas, affectuumque omnium perturbatio, perversitas et sinistra.
english: VIII. EVES penalty has four parts: multiplication of pain in childbirth, desire toward the husband, the husbands rule, and death. Adams penalty: the curse of the ground, labor in sweat, return to dust.

XI. As to the natural state, the force of nature was loosed and left to itself, and is no longer ruled and repressed by that peculiar providence of God by which under the state of innocence it was held back lest it bring any trouble on humans, as we taught above. As to the spiritual state, it is partly the loss of Gods first grace and favor, partly — what followed this — the grieving of Gods good Spirit and His departure from the human, which continuously the darkness of mind and ignorance or crookedness of will followed, and the disturbance, perversity, and sinister turn of all the affections.

title: XIII. From this fountain original sin and its unhappy brood; Liber III close toward Liber IV
latin: XIII. Ex hoc fonte et lerna malorum ad posteros Adae, qui secundum naturae modum ab eo descendunt, profluxit universale naturae nostrae vitium, quod nomine peccati originalis circumscribitur, cum omnimoda sua et infelici peccatorum poenarumque sobole, quam, veluti hydrae capita, nova gratia seminis benedicti in iis qui hoc fide viva recipiunt tandem salutariter praecidit. De peccato originis vidimus cap. 38; deque illius prole in sequentibus. Eius vero complexu Theologi tria potissimum intelligunt: 1. reatum utriusque mortis, qui in posteros transit triplici via, nempe (i) participatione culpae, quia omnes posteri in Adamo fuerunt seminali ratione, tanquam in capite seu radice, fonte ac communi principio totius naturae; (ii) imputatione, quia Adamus ita stabat in gratia ut, si peccaret, tota cum eo posteritas ea excideret; (iii) naturali propagatione, quia per generationem parentis rei conditionem participamus; 2. privationem divinae gratiae et defectum seu carentiam sapientiae, iustitiae et sanctimoniae; 3. horrendam in mente caliginem, in voluntate, affectibus totoque adeo homine ad peccandum pronitatem ac pravitatem. [Liber III COMPLETE. Liber IV PHYS 1005 De principiis et mediis humanae salutis; Cap. 1 De gratia paternae miserationis.]
english: XIII. From this fountain and Lerna of evils there flowed to Adams posterity, who descend from him according to the mode of nature, the universal fault of our nature, which is circumscribed by the name of original sin, with its whole and unhappy brood of sins and punishments, which — like the hydras heads — the new grace of the blessed seed at last cuts off savingly in those who receive this by living faith.

Of originating sin we saw in chapter 38; and of its brood in what follows. In its compass theologians chiefly understand three things: first, the guilt of both deaths, which passes to posterity by a triple way — namely (i) by participation of fault, because all posterity were in Adam by seminal reason, as in a head or root, fountain and common principle of the whole nature; (ii) by imputation, because Adam so stood in grace that if he sinned the whole posterity with him would fall from it; (iii) by natural propagation, because through the parents generation we share the condition of the guilty; second, the privation of divine grace and the defect or lack of wisdom, righteousness, and holiness; third, a horrible darkness in the mind, and in the will, affections, and so the whole human a proneness and crookedness toward sinning.
Book III COMPLETE. Book IV begins at physical page 1005 On the principles and means of human salvation; Chapter 1 On the grace of paternal compassion.
